title: Automate RBAC/policy bundle bootstrap for Private deployments (tenant isolation & bootstrap perms)
author: Aisha Patel
commits: Initial terraform bootstrap for RBAC bundles and tenant resources
Add Helm chart templates for rbac bundle and clusterrolebindings
Installer: wire bootstrapper to Terraform plan/apply and add idempotency checks
Add CI validation: validate-rbac.sh and e2e-helm job for private installer
Docs: private RBAC automation guide and rollback procedure
description:
Motivation: Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) require a reproducible, auditable bootstrap for RBAC and tenant isolation. Currently onboarding a new Private environment involves manual steps (apply Helm + multiple terraform scripts + ad-hoc clusterrolebindings) which is error-prone and blocks automation of upgrades/rollbacks. This PR implements automation to bootstrap RBAC policy bundles for Private deployments with explicit tenant isolation and least-privilege bootstrap permissions.

What this changes: Adds a Terraform module (terraform/modules/rbac-bundle) to manage policy bundle lifecycle, Helm templates (charts/redwood-private/templates/rbac.yaml) to render cluster- and namespace-scoped roles, and an installer bootstrapper (installer/bootstrapper/main.go) that coordinates plan/apply, validates idempotency, and records a checksum of the active bundle for safe upgrades. The RBAC policy artifacts are authored in rbac/policies (tenant_isolation.yaml and bootstrap-permissions.yaml). The CI pipeline gains validate-rbac.sh and an e2e helm verify job to catch regressions.

Design highlights: - Tenant isolation: namespaced Roles + explicit RoleBindings per-tenant, with a mininal cluster-admin-equivalent bootstrap role that is assigned only during initial bootstrap and then rotated/removed as part of normal ops. - Bootstrap permissions: bootstrap-permissions.yaml describes a narrowly-scoped service account and ClusterRole used only for initial resource provisioning. The installer records a bootstrap token and writes a one-time use marker to the cluster (ConfigMap with checksum) to prevent accidental re-exec. - Idempotency & upgrade safety: terraform module supports a `bundle_checksum` input; installer computes and compares checksums before attempting apply. Upgrades are gated by a dry-run plan step and an explicit `--force` flag for emergency rollouts. - Auditability: modules emit outputs for created RBAC resource names and a `policy_bundle_version` tag which is stored in cluster annotations.

Rollout plan: This is gated behind the Private installer feature flag. Steps tested in staging: 1) Run installer bootstrapper against a fresh cluster -> creates namespace per-tenant, applies policies, writes bundle checksum. 2) Re-run to validate idempotency (no changes). 3) Apply a bundle version bump (policy change) -> installer runs plan, shows diff, requires explicit confirmation in CLI for non-empty diffs. For existing Private customers we recommend running the bootstrapper in `--dry-run` mode first and then scheduling an off-peak maintenance window for the first apply.

Testing: Added unit tests for checksum logic and terraform plan parsing. Added an e2e Helm job (tests/e2e/helm/rbac-verify.yaml) that provisions a dev cluster and verifies tenant isolation constraints (no cross-namespace RoleBinding leakage). CI matrix includes: lint, unit, terraform-plan, e2e-helm. Some flakiness observed in e2e (networking in CI), we retried and stabilized the job by increasing timeouts.

Security review: Reviewed with Security (Riley Chen). Minor change: removed wildcard verbs from bootstrap ClusterRole and replaced with explicit verbs. No secrets are stored in the repo; bootstrapper supports KMS/HSM-backed tokens via environment variables.

Migration/upgrade notes: Existing customers will not be impacted until they opt into the new installer flow. For teams that have pre-existing manual RoleBindings, the installer supports an `--adopt` mode which will import and reconcile existing resources into the managed bundle (see docs/private/rbac-automation.md).

Rollback: The installer records a previous bundle checksum and terraform state is backed up in S3 (or customer-provided backend). To rollback, run `installer bootstrapper rollback --bundle CHECKSUM` which reverts Terraform state to the known good plan and reapplies last-known policies.

References: ENG-1324 for automation epic; SUP-778 for customer request.

release_notes: Private installer: automated RBAC/policy bundle bootstrap for private deployments. Adds a terraform module and Helm templates for managed RBAC bundles, installer orchestration for idempotent bootstrap, and CI validations. See docs/private/rbac-automation.md for usage and rollback instructions.
changelog_entry: Automated RBAC bootstrap for Private deployments: terraform module + Helm chart + installer integration; idempotent apply and bundle checksum support.
test_plan: Unit tests for checksum and plan parsing, CI terraform-plan validation, e2e helm test validating tenant isolation. Manual staging run completed.
notes_for_ops: Installer writes a ConfigMap named `rbac-bootstrap-<cluster>-meta` with `bundle_checksum` and `policy_bundle_version` annotations. To rollback use `installer bootstrapper rollback --bundle CHECKSUM`. Ensure terraform backend is reachable and state snapshots are enabled.
hotfix_related_incident: INC-2026-011 (customer failed onboarding due to missing clusterrolebindings)
